svg.title: Six hand types in training beat one: higher zero-shot success on an unseen hand
svg.desc: Dumbbell chart. For six held-out robot hands, zero-shot cube-picking success of policies trained on six other hands vs the average of policies trained on a single other hand: Sharpa 91% vs 42%; Wuji-2 77% vs 23%; Shadow 67% vs 46%; Allegro 60% vs 31%; Inspire 46% vs 37%; Wuji-1 42% vs 32%; LEAP 41% vs 13%.

g.text: Six hand types in training beat one: higher zero-shot success on an unseen hand

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #5c5c5c

g.text: A cube-picking policy is evaluated on a robot hand it never saw in training.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; fill: #5c5c5c

g.text: Final results, simulation (study closed). 90 evaluations (83 single-hand, 7 six-hand), 100 episodes each. Every model gets the same demonstration budget:

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; fill: #5c5c5c

g.text: 1,800 unique demonstration frames and 8,000 training updates. Single-hand: several source hands, up to 3 seeds; six-hand: 1 seed.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: Inter, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; fill: #5c5c5c

g.text: Six-hand training beats the single-hand average on 7/7 hands (+29 points on average); the single best source hand does as well or better on 3 of 7.
